items.title: Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom in 'fierce' battle to make chips at TSMC
items.author: Katie Tarasov
items.highlights: capacity is ‘fierce’ battleground for AI customers, amid record quarter Published Thu, Oct 15 2026 11:04 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 15 2026 12:56 PM EDT Katie Tarasov@KatieTarasov Key Points - TSMC makes the vast majority of the world's most advanced chips, but soaring AI demand has sparked fierce competition for manufacturing capacity. - Chip companies are cultivating relationships in Taiwan and making the case that they could become TSMC's next big customer. - At the center of the competition is TSMC executive Kevin Zhang, who one customer describes as "the most popular person on the planet."

items.title: Can robust TSMC earnings help settle AI jitters? By Investing.com
items.author: Senad Karaahmetovic
items.highlights: Investing.com - TSMC posted a $23.59 billion net profit for the third quarter of 2026, a 68.7% year-over-year surge that marked its sixth consecutive record quarter, yet the earnings beat has done little to arrest a deepening selloff across AI-linked semiconductor stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a foundry supplier to NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple, is the stock most exposed to AI hardware demand: its revenue is tied directly to the volume and complexity of chips ordered by hyperscalers and AI accelerator makers. items.title: TSMC ADRs Jump 2% as Nvidia Extends the Foundry Runway
items.author: Khac Phu Nguyen
items.highlights: at 1:06 PM EDT 1 min read Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), the world's largest contract chipmaker, delivered a tale of two markets Thursday. Taipei shares slipped 0.2%. Hours later, the U.S.-listed ADR jumped approximately 2.0% to $425.97 after Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) projected roughly 70% revenue growth next fiscal year. Taiwan closed before that bombshell. Wall Street did not miss it. TSMC hardly entered the rally empty-handed. July revenue rocketed 44.7% year over year to NT$467.58 billion.
